english: a hungry belly has no ears

evidence: Sen. Ep. 21.11: venter praecepta nōn audit: poscit, appellat
terms.comment: Literally “the belly does not listen to rules”: Seneca, of hunger, which demands its due like a creditor.
Literally “the belly has no ears”. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase. Seneca’s sentence says the same.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections, checked against the editions named there.
